# Defining-work questions and model rerun · 0.44

The earlier confirmation round sometimes withheld a plausible career because a novice could not confidently identify with technical terminology, a specialist task, or a secondary duty. This release asks whether the person would like to learn the profession’s central work.

## What changed

All117 professions now have two separately worded, plain-language defining-work questions. These are editorial learning-interest prompts informed by the linked O*NET occupational tasks, not additional validated assessment items. The official six interest totals and original field/task responses are unchanged.

Truck driving explicitly asks about driving a heavy truck and general load/road safety; hazardous goods transport is described as a specialty. Crop work asks about growing and caring for plants rather than selling them. Teaching asks about instruction and supporting learning rather than universal physical-development monitoring. Research questions cover inquiry, evidence and analysis without making custom programming a prerequisite. Software, professional scale and technical vocabulary are treated as things to learn.

Domain distinctions remain explicit. Animation asks about making animation, interpreting asks about meaning across languages, biomedical engineering asks about healthcare devices, occupational therapy asks about rehabilitation and everyday function, accounting asks about organizational financial records/reporting, and project management asks about accountable work-project delivery. Clinical responsibilities and safety remain part of those routes.

Two Yes answers with medium or high inference confidence can support defining work interest alongside the existing broader profile, task breadth, field and clinical-role checks. Low-confidence Yes, Unsure, Unfamiliar and No do not establish that interest. This removes the universal high-confidence inference requirement; it does not promote a career just for higher pay or degree willingness. Actual student responses remain direct responses, rather than simulated inferences.

## New answers, preserved history

The question bank and profession manifest were frozen before answer authoring. Three separate authors received only biographies and new question text, without earlier responses, review judgments, rankings or desired results. The authors supplied new responses, confidence and specific evidence for all154 models across655 profession checks (1,310 answers). All answers were frozen before the matching replay. Earlier0.41 comparisons,0.42 core-work answers and the0.43 qualitative review remain intact and independently reproducible.

These are fictional-profile simulations. A model’s inferred willingness is not recorded student behavior, a career choice or a claim of occupational aptitude. Uncertainty and author judgment remain visible for review.

## Rerun results

Across all154 models,131 now have at least one Top match, compared with79 before these fixes. There are229 Top offers (97 before);158 have a college or graduate route, including13 graduate-route offers.87 model Top lists changed. These are offer counts, so one model may have more than one qualifying profession.

Of the76 previously held offers,40 now qualify for Top and36 remain under Needs confirmation. Among the49 with college or graduate routes,22 qualify for Top and27 remain uncertain. All20 earlier strong-interest cases qualify;20 of42 plausible transfers qualify and22 remain uncertain. All14 earlier domain gaps remain unresolved. These are observed rerun results, not targets supplied to the answer authors.

Examples: Amina’s legal reasoning interests and Rojin’s information/research interests support medium-confidence learning transfers; Jules’s explicit dental observation and study exploration support dentistry. Grant’s interest in individual houses does not yet establish community land-use planning. Finley’s tutoring interest does not establish rehabilitation and everyday-function therapy. Their exact answers and evidence are available in the chart.

## Reading the chart

The pinned chart compares first matches with current Top matches. Expand the first column for the0.41 list and the Top list before these fixes. Open a model for all three answer rounds, evidence, route and budget details, or an isolated student preview. The earlier0.42 preview remains available separately.

The “76 previously held offers” filter retains the historical review cohort even when an offer now qualifies for Top. Its outcome list shows current status, the new defining-work answers and any unresolved question. The college and graduate filters apply to the current offers and the historical cohort.

Financial coverage still uses the first paid stage, the displayed gross-income threshold, monthly costs and savings, and prior-experience exclusions. Later illustrative pay cannot make an entry-stage lifestyle match.

See the current rerun counts and the public offer ledger in [the rerun validation](../validation/profession-interest-044.json). Six owner-only models and their new answer records remain in authenticated storage; their individual biographies and answers are excluded from public files.

## Validation

The release checks question/answer hashes, exact model and profession coverage, question-version separation, frozen original profiles and scores, historical Top lists, current chart/student agreement, education-filter behavior, clinical/profile safeguards, first-paid-stage affordability, and the owner-only data boundary. Browser review covers the updated cohort list, a degree filter, model history, an exact unresolved question and historical/current student previews.

Historical tests for the0.43 presentation-only release now read its saved baseline, since the0.44 rerun intentionally changes offers. The old0.42 high-confidence gate remains testable with its original versioned question bank.
